html:
Cyclone Winston struck Fiji on 20 February 2016 as the strongest tropical cyclone ever recorded in the Southern Hemisphere. It killed 44 people and destroyed tens of thousands of homes.

The storm's eye passed over the island of Koro and the north coast of Viti Levu, flattening whole villages. Damage equalled about a fifth of Fiji's yearly output.

Coming a year after Cyclone Pam in Vanuatu, it pushed Fiji to the front of Pacific campaigns on climate change. Fiji presided over the UN climate talks in 2017, and began moving coastal villages inland. See also Fiji.
